prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (2005–2010)

Economy and taxation
- Add higher progressive income tax bands; introduce more corporation tax bands with higher rates for larger firms.
- Increase taxes on unearned wealth; reform inheritance tax to be paid by recipients; abolish National Insurance and raise equivalent revenue from all income.
- Pilot a land value tax to replace council tax and uniform business rates.
- Phase out VAT and introduce revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes on resource use, pollution and waste (including measures such as an aviation fuel tax and charges on single‑use items).
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies; support small businesses and co‑operatives; oppose entry to the euro; reform trade rules.
- Job creation via renewables, low‑carbon transport and zero‑waste industries; uphold union rights; reduce working hours; remove employers’ NIC; adopt broader well‑being metrics beyond GDP.

Energy and climate
- Adopt a Contraction and Convergence framework with emissions cuts of 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020 and 85% by 2030.
- Replace domestic energy VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a carbon tax based on fuel carbon content; abolish standing charges and use progressive tariffs.
- Reach 40% of energy from renewables by 2020; invest in solar, wind, wave and biogas; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; decommission nuclear plants at end of life.
- Reduce demand via a Warmer Homes Act (30% cut in domestic use in 10 years) and local “Smart Energy Councils”; cabinet‑level lead on climate policy.

Welfare, housing, work and families
- Phase in a universal Citizen’s Income replacing most means‑tested benefits (disability/incapacity retained; housing benefit initially separate).
- Introduce a universal, earnings‑linked Citizen’s Pension replacing pension credit.
- Simplify child support and increase child benefit; end the Working Time Directive opt‑out and explore a 35‑hour average week; expand early‑years centres.
- Boost affordable housing: allow councils to reinvest sales receipts; support self‑build co‑ops; use LVT; upgrade insulation and efficiency.

Health and education
- Restore universal, comprehensive NHS provision; end private finance mechanisms and resist trade liberalisation of public services.
- Abolish prescription charges; restore free eye tests and NHS dental care; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Raise health funding to about 9% of GNP; consider a dedicated NHS tax; redirect future defence savings.
- Increase education funding; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs and move toward individual learning plans; expand pre‑school provision.

Transport
- Cut road traffic 10% by 2010; shift £30bn from road building to public transport; re‑regulate buses; integrated ticketing; planning for walking/cycling and mixed‑use areas.
- Return rail and underground systems to public ownership; expand rail, freight, and light rail.
- Reflect full motoring costs via congestion/road pricing and higher fuel duty; abolish the tax disc; incentivise cleaner freight; fund R&D for efficient vehicles.
- Restrain aviation growth: oppose airport expansion, ban night flights, tax aviation fuel EU‑wide; tax domestic flight emissions; raise passenger duty; shift short trips to rail.

Environment, food and farming
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration; cut packaging; set recycled‑content standards; 60% household recycling by 2010; create a Zero Waste Agency.
- Establish an Environmental Protection Commission; expand eco‑taxes on harmful inputs; strengthen chemical regulation; promote biodegradable alternatives.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation and nanotechnology; oppose patents on genetic resources; strengthen animal welfare (e.g., end live exports, ban battery eggs and fur imports).
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local food chains.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies for organics, biodiversity and sustainable rural incomes; ban GM food; tighten supermarket Code of Practice with independent oversight.

Crime and justice
- Prevention via urban design, youth services, rapid repairs, visible staff; treat drug misuse as a health issue; oppose ID cards and redirect funds to prevention.
- Expand community policing, local stations and oversight; strengthen independent complaints system.
- Tighten gun laws (clear lethality thresholds, broader prohibitions, single licensing with competence and mental‑health checks; standing advisory committee).
- Expand restorative justice; enhance responses to hate crime and violence against women; back stronger disability rights.

Democracy and constitutional reform
- Oppose national ID cards.
- Devolve power to local and regional government; introduce proportional representation locally and for Westminster; enable recall and local referenda.
- Create an elected second chamber by PR; draft a written constitution; disestablish the state church; limit monarchical roles.
- Reform regional governance and consider further devolution in Scotland and Wales subject to public consent.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while advocating a more democratic, transparent EU.

International policy
- Pursue an ethical foreign policy; withdraw troops from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers.
- Reduce defence spending to the EU average; end arms‑export subsidies; back an Arms Trade Treaty; decommission nuclear weapons; renounce WMD.
- Increase aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; support Tobin tax and equitable carbon trading.
- Reform the UN (abolish permanent Security Council seats, majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Reform global trade rules to permit localisation and sustainability (e.g., a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade).
- Improve asylum policy: timely decisions, right to work and benefits, independent appeals; ratify the 1990 UN migrant workers convention; uphold the 1951 Refugee Convention.
